idiom_name: method composed of private helper-method calls
implementation_notes: Ruby method bodies are message sends, and the Smalltalk-derived style this catalog's method patterns come from is native here: the coordinator sends messages to self without a receiver and the steps are declared after private so they cannot be called from outside. Since Ruby 2.7 a private method may also be invoked with a literal self. receiver, so self-prefixed calls stay legal without widening visibility; protected is a different, wider boundary (other instances of the same class).
code_sketch:
class Checkout
  def run                      # the body is only calls
    return -1 unless reserve_stock
    return -1 unless charge_card
    send_receipt
    0
  end

  private
  def reserve_stock; true; end
end
pitfalls: private applies to everything that follows in the class body: a helper added after the keyword becomes private (and one added before it stays public), so method order silently controls visibility.
Private methods cannot be called with an arbitrary receiver: other.reserve_stock raises NoMethodError even when other is the same class - only no receiver or a literal self is allowed.
Messages resolve at runtime, so a misspelled step is caught only when the coordinator runs, and method_missing (from metaprogramming or a decorator library) can absorb the call instead of failing.
